His second son Daifeng rose under Gaozong to general of the Left Leopard-Strategy Guard.
豹韜 is the Leopard Strategy guard (Bao Tao). 韜 does not mean bow.
The second son Daifeng, in Gaozong's time, reached office as General of the Left Leopard Bow Guard.
The second son Daifeng, in Gaozong's time, reached office as General of the Left Leopard-Strategy Guard.
豹韜 is the Leopard Strategy guard (Bao Tao). 韜 does not mean bow.
Jian was a cousin of Emperor Gaozu on the maternal side.
Jian was a collateral nephew of Emperor Gaozu.
從甥 is a lower-generation collateral nephew. It is not a same-generation cousin, and the Chinese does not say maternal.
Jian was Gaozu's maternal nephew's son.
從甥 does not spell out a maternal nephew's son. 從 marks collateral distance and 甥 marks the nephew generation; 'maternal' is not in the text.
He was later made acting governor of Shengzhou but resigned to observe mourning for his mother.
He was later made acting military governor of Shengzhou but resigned to observe mourning for his mother.
都督 is a military governor. The idiomatic 'governor' drops that rank. 檢校 means the appointment was acting.
The court debated sending troops, but instead recalled Jian as envoy to investigate the situation on the spot.
The court debated sending troops, and also appointed Jian as envoy to investigate the situation on the spot.
仍 means the court still, or in addition, raised Jian as envoy while debating an attack. It does not say the attack was dropped in his place.
He was promptly made acting governor of Daizhou.
He was promptly made acting military governor of Daizhou.
代州都督 is military governor of Daizhou, and 檢校 means acting. 'Governor' alone understates the office.
He was transferred to governor of Yingzhou and made protector of the Eastern Yi.
He was transferred to military governor of Yingzhou and concurrently made Colonel Protector of the Eastern Yi.
都督 is a military governor, 兼 marks a concurrent post, and 護東夷校尉 is Colonel Protector of the Eastern Yi. The idiomatic text drops both the military rank and the colonelcy.

Under Tang custom, officials of third rank and above displayed ceremonial halberds at their gates. All three Zhang brothers' households bore them, and contemporaries honoured them as "the Zhang family of three halberds."

Under Tang regulations, officials of third rank and above displayed ceremonial halberds at their gates. All three Zhang brothers' households bore them, and contemporaries honoured them as "the Zhang family of three halberds."
唐製 means Tang regulations or institutional rules, not merely custom.
His father Yong, at the end of the Sui, led several thousand local men in suppressing bandits on behalf of the prefecture.
His father Yong, at the end of the Daye era, led several thousand local men in suppressing bandits on behalf of the prefecture.
大業末 names the Daye era. The idiomatic text replaces that era name with the dynasty alone.
Dingfang was ferociously strong and utterly fearless. Before he was fifteen he rode with his father on punitive expeditions, always first over the wall and into the enemy ranks.
Dingfang was ferociously strong and utterly fearless. When he was a little over ten he rode with his father on punitive expeditions, always first over the wall and into the enemy ranks.
年十餘歲 means a little over ten years old. It does not state an upper limit of fifteen.
Yaxian soon again for Liu Heidan attacked and took cities and towns; Dingfang every time had military achievement.
Yaxian soon again, on behalf of Liu Heidan, attacked and took cities and towns; Dingfang every time had military achievement.
為劉黑闥 means on Liu Heidan's behalf. The literal 'for Liu Heidan attacked' is not grammatical English.
Early in Zhenguan he became a frontier colonel of Kuangdao and joined Li Jing's surprise attack on the Turk qaghan Jieli at Qikou.
Early in Zhenguan he became a frontier colonel of Kuangdao and joined Li Jing's surprise attack on the Turk Jieli at Qikou.
The Chinese says 突厥頡利 and does not call him qaghan in this sentence.
At the beginning of Zhenguan he was Colonel Who Breaks the Ranks of Kuangdao prefecture, following Li Jing in the surprise attack on the Turk Jieli at Qikou.
At the beginning of Zhenguan he was Colonel Who Breaks the Ranks of the Kuangdao fu, following Li Jing in the surprise attack on the Turk Jieli at Qikou.
匡道府 is a garrison fu, not a prefecture.
When the army returned, he was appointed Central Commander of the Left Martial Guard.
When the army returned, he was appointed Commandant of the Left Martial Guard.
中郎將 is the office of commandant, not a 'central commander'.
During Yonghui he was transferred to the Left Guard and joined Grand General Cheng Zhijie in the campaign against Helu as commander of the vanguard.

During Yonghui he was transferred to Commandant of the First Merit Garrison of the Left Guard and followed Grand General of the Left Guard Cheng Zhijie in the campaign against Helu as commander of the vanguard.
左衛勳一府中郎將 is a specific commandancy. The idiomatic text reduces it to a transfer 'to the Left Guard' and drops 左衛 from Cheng Zhijie's rank.
The yabghu Nandulu submitted with more than ten thousand tents of his people. Dingfang received them kindly, then took a thousand of their horsemen and pressed on into Turgish territory.
The irkin Nandulu submitted with more than ten thousand tents of his people. Dingfang received them kindly, then took a thousand of their horsemen and pressed on into Turgish territory.
俟斤 is the Turkic title irkin, not yabghu (葉護).
Their yabghu Nandulu came to surrender with more than ten thousand tents of followers; Dingfang comforted them, then sent forth a thousand of their horsemen and advanced to the Turgish division.
Their irkin Nandulu came to surrender with more than ten thousand tents of followers; Dingfang comforted them, then sent forth a thousand of their horsemen and advanced to the Turgish division.
俟斤 is the Turkic title irkin, not yabghu (葉護).

Helu mustered nearly one hundred thousand men from the Holuwi, Shefat, Shunishi Chuban, and Chumukun Qulu yabghus and the On Ok confederation to block the imperial army. Dingfang led a force of more than ten thousand Uyghur and Han troops against them.

Helu mustered nearly one hundred thousand men from the Holuwi, Shefat, Shunishi Chuban, and Chumukun Qulu chuo chiefs and the On Ok confederation to block the imperial army. Dingfang led a force of more than ten thousand Uyghur and Han troops against them.
The leaders' titles are 啜 (chuo), not yabghu.

Helu led the forces of the Holuwi yabghu, Shefat yabghu, Shunishi Chuban yabghu, Chumukun Qulu yabghu, and the On Ok confederation — troops numbering nearly one hundred thousand — to resist the imperial army; Dingfang led more than ten thousand Uyghurs and Han soldiers to attack them.

Helu led the forces of the Holuwi chuo, Shefat chuo, Shunishi Chuban chuo, Chumukun Qulu chuo, and the On Ok confederation — troops numbering nearly one hundred thousand — to resist the imperial army; Dingfang led more than ten thousand Uyghurs and Han soldiers to attack them.
Each title in the Chinese is 啜 (chuo), not yabghu.
Holuwi and the other On Ok leaders then surrendered with their full forces. Helu alone fled west with the Chumukun Qulu yabghu and a few hundred horsemen.
Holuwi and the other five Nushibi then surrendered with their full forces. Helu alone fled west with the Chumukun Qulu chuo and a few hundred horsemen.
五努失畢 are the five Nushibi, not the On Ok (ten arrows). 啜 is the title chuo, not yabghu (葉護).
Thereupon Holuwi and the rest of the On Ok submitted with all their forces; Helu alone fled west with Chumukun Qulu yabghu and several hundred horsemen.
Thereupon Holuwi and the rest of the five Nushibi submitted with all their forces; Helu alone fled west with the Chumukun Qulu chuo and several hundred horsemen.
五努失畢 are the five Nushibi, not the On Ok. 屈律啜 is a chuo title, not yabghu.
For his achievements Dingfang was promoted to Grand General of the Left Xiaoqi Guard and enfeoffed as Duke of Xing. His son Qingjie was enfeoffed as Duke of Wuyi County.
For his achievements Dingfang was promoted to Grand General of the Left Xiaowei Guard and enfeoffed as Duke of Xing. His son Qingjie was enfeoffed as Duke of Wuyi County.
左驍衛 is the Xiaowei Guard. Xiaoqi would be 驍騎, which is not the text.
For his merit Dingfang was transferred to Grand General of the Left Xiaoqi Guard, enfeoffed as Duke of Xing State, and his son Qingjie was also enfeoffed as Duke of Wuyi County.
For his merit Dingfang was transferred to Grand General of the Left Xiaowei Guard, enfeoffed as Duke of Xing State, and his son Qingjie was also enfeoffed as Duke of Wuyi County.
左驍衛 is the Xiaowei Guard, not the Xiaoqi cavalry.

Soon afterward the Sijie yabghu Dudman, who had once governed the western tribes, rallied his own people together with Kashgar, Jujpan, and the Onion Range and rebelled again. Dingfang was appointed Pacification Commissioner and ordered to lead an expedition against them.

Soon afterward the Sijie irkin Dudman, who had once governed the western tribes, rallied his own people together with Kashgar, Jujpan, and the Onion Range and rebelled again. Dingfang was appointed Pacification Commissioner and ordered to lead an expedition against them.
闕俟斤 is an irkin title (俟斤), not yabghu (葉護).

Soon the Sijie yabghu Dudman, who had formerly governed the various barbarians, gathered his following together with the three states of Kashgar, Jujpan, and the Onion Range and rebelled again; an edict appointed Dingfang Pacification Commissioner and ordered him to lead troops to suppress them.

Soon the Sijie irkin Dudman, who had formerly governed the various barbarians, gathered his following together with the three states of Kashgar, Jujpan, and the Onion Range and rebelled again; an edict appointed Dingfang Pacification Commissioner and ordered him to lead troops to suppress them.
闕俟斤 is an irkin title, not yabghu.
Seeing no way out, Dudman came out with his face bound in surrender.
Seeing no way out, Dudman came out and surrendered with his hands bound behind his back.
面縛 means surrender with the hands tied behind the back, not binding the face.
Dudman, knowing he could not escape, bound his own face and opened the gate to come out and surrender.
Dudman, knowing he could not escape, bound his hands behind his back and opened the gate to come out and surrender.
面縛 is hands bound behind the back, not a bound face.

Dingfang returned with his captive to the Eastern Capital. Emperor Gaozong received him at Qianyang Hall, and Dingfang presented Dudman before the throne. All lands west of the Onion Range were now pacified.

Dingfang returned with his captive to the Eastern Capital. Emperor Gaozong received him at Qianyang Hall, and Dingfang presented the tegin Dudman before the throne. All lands west of the Onion Range were now pacified.
都曼特勒 includes the title 特勒 (tegin). The idiomatic sentence drops it.

With the captive he returned to the Eastern Capital; Emperor Gaozong attended at Qianyang Hall, and Dingfang led the captive Dudman forward to present him; west of the Onion Range was entirely pacified.

With the captive he returned to the Eastern Capital; Emperor Gaozong attended at Qianyang Hall, and Dingfang led the tegin Dudman forward to present him; west of the Onion Range was entirely pacified.
都曼特勒 includes the title 特勒 (tegin), which the literal omits.

Uija's second son Tai declared himself king. The legitimate heir Wensii said, "The king and crown prince may have left the city, but they are still alive. My uncle has seized command and made himself king. If the Tang army withdraws, my father and I will not survive."

Uija's second son Tai declared himself king. The legitimate heir Wensii said, "The king and crown prince may have left the city, but they are still alive. My uncle has seized command and made himself king. If the Han army withdraws, my father and I will not survive."
漢兵 means the Han army. The idiomatic text substitutes Tang, which the Chinese does not say.

When the main army besieged Andi, the Goguryeo regent Yeon Gaesomun sent Generals Gao Yanshou and Gao Huizhen with two hundred fifty thousand men to meet them. The enemy encamped on the hills, and Taizong ordered his generals to attack from all four sides.

When the main army besieged Andi, the Goguryeo mangniji sent Generals Gao Yanshou and Gao Huizhen with two hundred fifty thousand men to meet them. The enemy encamped on the hills, and Taizong ordered his generals to attack from all four sides.
莫離支 is the Goguryeo title mangniji. The idiomatic text adds the personal name Yeon Gaesomun, which this sentence does not give.

When the great army attacked Andi City, the Goguryeo regent Yeon Gaesomun sent generals Gao Yanshou and Gao Huizhen leading two hundred fifty thousand troops to resist battle; they encamped relying on the hills, and Taizong divided orders among the generals to attack on four sides.

When the great army attacked Andi City, the Goguryeo mangniji sent generals Gao Yanshou and Gao Huizhen leading two hundred fifty thousand troops to resist battle; they encamped relying on the hills, and Taizong divided orders among the generals to attack on four sides.
莫離支 is a title, not the personal name Yeon Gaesomun. The literal inserts a name the Chinese does not use.
The Nishu tribe, allied with Sugan, refused to submit to Helu. Helu defeated them and seized their wives and children.
Nishu, relying on his own plain ability, refused to submit to Helu. The bandits defeated him and seized his wives and children.
仗素幹 means relying on one's own plain ability. Sugan is not a person, and 泥熟 is not called a tribe here.
Now the Nishu, relying on Sugan, would not submit to Helu; they were broken by the bandits, who captured their wives and children.
Now Nishu, relying on his own plain ability, would not submit to Helu; they were broken by the bandits, who captured their wives and children.
仗素幹 means relying on plain ability. The literal turns 素幹 into a person named Sugan.
Our soldiers have taken Nishu families from among Helu's tribes and plan to keep them as bondsmen. These captives should be found and returned, with gifts added as compensation.
Han soldiers have taken Nishu families from among Helu's tribes and plan to keep them as bondsmen. These captives should be found and returned, with gifts added as compensation.
漢兵 means the Han soldiers. The idiomatic text substitutes Our, which the Chinese does not say.
A Goguryeo marksman below Shicheng had killed more than ten Tang soldiers. Rengui charged him alone. The man's bow failed, his hands went limp, and Rengui took him alive.
A Goguryeo marksman below Shicheng had killed more than ten men. Rengui charged him alone. The man's bow failed, his hands went limp, and Rengui took him alive.
十餘人 does not say Tang. The idiomatic sentence adds Tang.
At the beginning of Qianfeng, the Goguryeo general Cheon Gwon Yeon defected with his forces. Gaozong sent Generals Pang Tongshan and Gao to receive him.
At the beginning of Qianfeng, the Goguryeo general Quan Nansheng defected with his forces. Gaozong sent Generals Pang Tongshan, Gao, and others to receive him.
泉男生 is Quan Nansheng; Cheon Gwon Yeon does not transcribe those characters. 高等 means Gao and others, which the idiomatic text drops.
At the beginning of Qianfeng, the Goguryeo grand general Cheon Gwon Yeon led his masses in internal submission; Gaozong sent Generals Pang Tongshan and Gao to welcome him.
At the beginning of Qianfeng, the Goguryeo grand general Quan Nansheng led his masses in internal submission; Gaozong sent Generals Pang Tongshan, Gao, and others to welcome him.
泉男生 is Quan Nansheng, not Cheon Gwon Yeon, and 高等 includes others besides Gao.
Yeon's younger brother Yeon-geon rallied the kingdom's forces to attack Pang Tongshan. Rengui was ordered to bring up the rear with reinforcements.
Nansheng's younger brother Nanjian rallied the kingdom's forces to attack Pang Tongshan and the others. Rengui was ordered to bring up the rear with reinforcements.
男建 is Nanjian, not Yeon-geon, and 同善等 includes Tongshan and the others.
Yeon's younger brother Yeon-geon led the people of the state to strike back against Tongshan and the others; an edict ordered Rengui to command troops as rear support.
Nansheng's younger brother Nanjian led the people of the state to strike back against Tongshan and the others; an edict ordered Rengui to command troops as rear support.
男建 reads Nanjian. Yeon-geon drops 男 and adds a surname the clause does not write.
In 670, when Tibet invaded, Rengui was again appointed grand commander of the Luosa Route army.
In the first year of Xianheng, when Tibet invaded, Rengui was again appointed grand commander of the Luosa Route army.
咸亨元年 is the first year of Xianheng. The idiomatic text drops the era name and leaves only a Western year.
Tibet sent another four hundred thousand men to give battle. The Tang army suffered a crushing defeat, and Rengui negotiated a truce with the Tibetan general Lun Qinling.
Tibet sent another four hundred thousand men to give battle. The government army suffered a crushing defeat, and Rengui negotiated a truce with the Tibetan general Lun Qinling.
官軍 is the government army. The idiomatic text substitutes Tang, which the Chinese does not say.
Missing his past service, Gaozong summoned him again in 681 and said, "When the flood hit Jiucheng Palace, I would have drowned if not for you.
Missing his past service, Gaozong summoned him again in the first year of Kaiyao and said, "When the flood hit Jiucheng Palace, I would have drowned if not for you.
開耀元年 is the first year of Kaiyao. The idiomatic text drops the era name.

The emperor restored him as chief administrator of Guazhou, then promoted him to general of the Right Leading Army Guard and acting military governor of Daizhou. He led troops against the Türk leader Yuan Zhen at Yunzhou, taking more than ten thousand heads, twenty thousand captives, and over thirty thousand camels, horses, cattle, and sheep.

The emperor restored him as chief administrator of Guazhou, then promoted him to general of the Right Leading Army Guard and acting military governor of Daizhou. He led troops against the Türk leader Yuan Zhen and others at Yunzhou, taking more than ten thousand heads, twenty thousand captives, and over thirty thousand camels, horses, cattle, and sheep.
元珍等 means Yuan Zhen and others. The idiomatic sentence drops 等.

Thereupon he was restored and appointed Long Secretary of Guazhou; soon he was made General of the Right Leading Army Guard, acting Military Governor of Daizhou; again he led troops to attack the Türks Yuan Zhen and others at Yun Prefecture, beheading over ten thousand, capturing over twenty thousand captives, and over thirty thousand camels, horses, cattle, and sheep.

Thereupon he was restored and appointed Chief Secretary of Guazhou; soon he was made General of the Right Leading Army Guard, acting Military Governor of Daizhou; again he led troops to attack the Türks Yuan Zhen and others at Yun Prefecture, beheading over ten thousand, capturing over twenty thousand captives, and over thirty thousand camels, horses, cattle, and sheep.
長史 is the office of chief secretary (changshi). Long Secretary misreads 長 as the English word long.
His father Cheng Mingzhen served Dou Jiande as magistrate of Pule at the end of the Sui. He was so capable that local rebels did not dare touch his district.
His father Cheng Mingzhen served Dou Jiande as magistrate of Pule at the end of the Daye era. He was so capable that local rebels did not dare touch his district.
大業末 names the Daye era. The idiomatic text broadens it to the end of the Sui.
He soon abandoned Jiande and returned to Tang allegiance. Gaozu appointed him magistrate of Yongnian by remote commission and ordered him to lead troops in pacifying Hebei.
He soon abandoned Jiande and returned to the realm. Gaozu appointed him magistrate of Yongnian by remote commission and ordered him to lead troops in pacifying Hebei.
歸國 says he returned to the realm. The idiomatic text adds Tang.
When Liu Heita soon captured Ming Prefecture, Mingzhen and Prefect Chen Junbin fought their way out and returned to the Tang court.
When Liu Heita soon captured Ming Prefecture, Mingzhen and Prefect Chen Junbin extricated themselves and returned to court.
自拔歸朝 means they extricated themselves and returned to court. The idiomatic text adds a fight and the name Tang.

Mingzhen joined Taizong's campaign against Heita. While Heita was moving supplies by land and water through Ji, Bei, Cang, and Ying to block the Tang army, Mingzhen led a thousand men in ambush and destroyed every boat and wagon.

Mingzhen joined Taizong's campaign against Heita. While Heita was moving supplies by land and water through Ji, Bei, Cang, and Ying to block the government army, Mingzhen led a thousand men in ambush and destroyed every boat and wagon.
官軍 is the government army, not the word Tang.
In 655 he was appointed military governor of Ying Prefecture and concurrently Protector-General of the Eastern Barbarians.
In the sixth year of Yonghui he was appointed military governor of Ying Prefecture and concurrently Protector-General of the Eastern Barbarians.
永徽六年 is the sixth year of Yonghui. The idiomatic text drops the era name.
In the sixth year of Yonghui he was cumulatively removed as Military Governor of Ying Prefecture, concurrently Eastern Barbarians Protector.
In the sixth year of Yonghui he was successively appointed Military Governor of Ying Prefecture, concurrently Eastern Barbarians Protector.
除 in an appointment notice means he was appointed, not removed.
He also defeated Goguryeo at the Guiduan River, burned their new city, and inflicted heavy casualties.
He also defeated Goguryeo at the Guiduan River, burned Xincheng, and inflicted heavy casualties.
新城 is the city Xincheng, already named that way in this chapter, not a newly built city.
Again he led troops to break Goguryeo at Guiduan River, burned their new city, and killed and captured in great numbers.
Again he led troops to break Goguryeo at Guiduan River, burned Xincheng, and killed and captured in great numbers.
新城 is the place Xincheng. The literal renders it as a newly built city.
He died in 662. He was posthumously made grand general of the Right Guard and given the posthumous name Lie ("Fierce").
He died in the second year of Longshuo. He was posthumously made grand general of the Right Guard and given the posthumous name Lie ("Fierce").
龍朔二年 is the second year of Longshuo. The idiomatic text drops the era name.
During the Yonglong era, the Türk leader Shifunian rebelled. The Dingxiang Route commanders Li Wenjian, Cao Huaishun, and Dou Yizhao were defeated one after another.
During the Yonglong era, the Türk leader Shi Funian rebelled. The Dingxiang Route commanders Li Wenjian, Cao Huaishun, and Dou Yizhao and others were defeated one after another.
史伏念 is Shi Funian, not one word Shifunian. 等 means the commanders and others, which the idiomatic sentence drops.

In 683, Bai Tieyu of Chenping County in Sui Prefecture led the followers of tribal chief Qizhi in seizing the county seat. He declared himself a ruler, appointed a full bureaucracy, and raided Suixi, killing officials, looting the countryside, and burning villages. The court ordered Wuting and Wang Fangyi, military governor of Xia Prefecture, to crush the rebellion.

In the second year of Yongchun, Bai Tieyu of Chenping County in Sui Prefecture led a band of the Buluoji in seizing the county seat. He declared himself a ruler, appointed a full bureaucracy, and raided Suixi, killing officials, looting the countryside, and burning villages. The court ordered Wuting and Wang Fangyi, military governor of Xia Prefecture, to crush the rebellion.
永淳二年 is the second year of Yongchun. 部落稽 is the Buluoji people, not a chief named Qizhi.

In the second year of Yongchun, Bai Tieyu of Chenping County, Sui Prefecture, led the party of tribal chief Qizhi to seize the county seat and rebel; he falsely assumed an honorific title, appointed officials, and further invaded Suixi, killing and plundering officials and people, burning villages; an edict ordered Wuting and Military Governor of Xia Prefecture Wang Fangyi to suppress them.

In the second year of Yongchun, Bai Tieyu of Chenping County, Sui Prefecture, led a band of the Buluoji to seize the county seat and rebel; he falsely assumed an honorific title, appointed officials, and further invaded Suixi, killing and plundering officials and people, burning villages; an edict ordered Wuting and Military Governor of Xia Prefecture Wang Fangyi to suppress them.
部落稽 is the Buluoji people. The literal invents a tribal chief named Qizhi from the character 稽.
At the end of the Sui he gathered a band of raiders and attacked towns across the region. People far and near feared them, and they were known as the Huyu Bandits.
At the end of the Daye era he gathered a band of raiders and attacked towns across the region. People far and near feared them, and they were known as the Huyu Bandits.
大業末 names the Daye era. The idiomatic text broadens it to the end of the Sui.
In 633, returning from a campaign against rebellious Liao tribes, Taizong praised him: "I hear you took arrows and stones in person and led from the front. What ancient general could do more?

In the seventh year of Zhenguan, returning from a campaign against rebellious Liao tribes, Taizong praised him: "I hear you took arrows and stones in person and led from the front. What ancient general could do more?
貞觀七年 is the seventh year of Zhenguan. The idiomatic text drops the era name.
Guo, Xue, and Cheng staked everything on desperate feats of arms.
Guo, Xue, and Wuting staked everything on desperate feats of arms.
務挺 is the given name Wuting. The idiomatic line substitutes the surname Cheng.
candidateDispositions: English Qizhi here is a mistranslation of 部落稽 (the Buluoji), not Cheng Wuting's son Qizhi in s0262.

unresolvedReferences.description: Taizong says three generals differ in worth. The owned text names Guo Xiaoke in the next sentence and has just described Ashina She'er refusing gifts; it does not identify the third general.
